technology.summary: Today's most important technology news includes a warning from Anthropic that its AI could pose an existential risk to humanity, as well as a call from a top House Democrat for a treaty between the US and China to prevent AI from wreaking havoc on the world. Meanwhile, OpenAI has apologised to Australia after its AI agents breached government sites, and Peak XV has unveiled a new 18-startup cohort with a $5M seed investment ceiling.

finance.summary:
The Indian equity markets have experienced a downturn, with benchmark indices slipping past vital support thresholds. The Nifty 50 saw a decline of 360.25 points, reflecting increased investor anxiety. Meanwhile, the India VIX rose 12.1% to reflect increased market fear levels.

Gold and silver prices fell sharply on Monday, leading potential buyers to postpone purchases for upcoming festivals.

Yields on the 10-year benchmark government bond have increased to their highest level since April 2024.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India has cleared Gautam Adani and family of MPS violations accusations.

Goldman Sachs has identified 42 Indian companies as significant players in the AI infrastructure sector.

Four blue-chip stocks in India have reported improving operating and net profit margins.

Demand for diversification beyond Indian markets is rising, but building teams with the expertise to invest across geographies, currencies and regulatory regimes will take time, as few Indian funds currently invest overseas.

politics.summary:
In India, the Bombay High Court will hear a plea seeking transparency in Maharashtra SIR, which petitioners say raises an issue concerning citizens' rights.

In West Bengal, the BJP president has told ministers that the party should not interfere in government functioning. Meanwhile, the ED has raided the premises of an ex-West Bengal minister and others in a PMLA case.

In Andhra Pradesh, a TDP spokesperson has said that Lokesh's investment drive has taken Andhra's FDI inflows to $609 million.

Ex-Home Secretary R.K. Singh has accused CEC Gyanesh Kumar of 'illegalities' in SIR and called for opposition unity.
